source_caption:
The hilariously toxic, co-dependent relationship between Tom Wambsgans and “Cousin” Greg Hirsch was often just as chaotic behind the scenes. Actors Matthew Macfadyen and Nicholas Braun found each other so naturally funny that they became notoriously incapable of keeping a straight face during takes. Their habit of “corpsing” (a theatrical term for breaking character to laugh) became such a massive disruption on set that Macfadyen was widely known among the cast and crew as the worst offender. The problem was so severe that showrunner Jesse Armstrong occasionally had to playfully threaten to separate the two actors like unruly schoolchildren, just so they could successfully finish filming their absurd, insult-laden scenes without bursting into uncontrollable giggles.

Succession (2018–2023), created by Jesse Armstrong, starring Brian Cox, Jeremy Strong, Kieran Culkin, Sarah Snook, Matthew Macfadyen, Nicholas Braun. The aging, tyrannical patriarch of a global media and entertainment conglomerate begins to step back from the company, sparking a vicious, high-stakes battle for control among his four wealthy, deeply dysfunctional children.

source_details.synopsis: Succession is an American satirical comedy-drama television series created by English screenwriter Jesse Armstrong that aired for four seasons on HBO from June 3, 2018, to May 28, 2023. The series centers on the Roy family, the owners of global media and entertainment conglomerate Waystar RoyCo, and their fight for control of the company amidst uncertainty about the health of the family's patriarch. Brian Cox portrays the family patriarch Logan Roy. His children are played by Alan Ruck as Connor, Jeremy Strong as Kendall, Kieran Culkin as Roman, and Sarah Snook as Shiv.
